title: Regular Taylor minors and the finite-value equality germ
statement:
Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field, $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ a smooth finite-type $k$-scheme with an etale coordinate map $x:U\to\mathbf A_k^d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_s\in R$ generate an ideal $I$ defining a closed subscheme $X\subset U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $\partial_j$ for the $k$-derivation extending $\partial/\partial x_j$, and $\partial^\nu$ for its iterates. At $b\in U$, let $L_b=\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and let $\tau_b:R\to L_b[[T_1,\ldots,T_d]]$ be the centered Taylor homomorphism sending $x_j$ to $x_j(b)+T_j$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Put $K_b=(\tau_b(h_1),\ldots,\tau_b(h_s))$ and $H_b(t)=\dim_{L_b}L_b[[T]]/(K_b+(T)^{t+1})$. Thus $H_b$ uses all $d$ relative variables, also at nonclosed points. For $t\ge0$, form a regular matrix $P_t(h)$ whose rows are multiindices $|\gamma|\le t$ and columns are $(i,\eta)$, $|\eta|\le t$, with entry zero when $\eta\not\le\gamma$ and otherwise $\partial^{\gamma-\eta}h_i/(\gamma-\eta)!$. Fix $a\in U$, put $r_t(a)=\operatorname{rank}_{L_a}P_t(h)(a)$ and let $J_t(a)\subset R$ be the ideal of its $(r_t(a)+1)$-minors [def-trf-minor-ideal]. The Taylor image of $P_t(h)$ at $a$ is the matrix of $Y^\eta\tau_a(h_i)(T+Y)\bmod(Y)^{t+1}$, and the extension of $J_t(a)$ under $\tau_a$ is its ideal of $(r_t(a)+1)$-minors. Each $J_t(a)$ is independent of the finite regular generators $h_i$ of $I$. Suppose the functions $H_b$ take only finitely many distinct values on some neighbourhood of $a$. Then there is $q_0\ge0$ such that for every $q\ge q_0$ there is an open neighbourhood $V_q$ of $a$ with
$$\{b\in V_q:J_t(a)\subseteq\ker(R\to L_b)\text{ for every }0\le t\le q\}=\{b\in V_q:H_b=H_a\}.$$
Thus these ideals give the extended Hilbert--Samuel equality germ as a set. Empty generator families, zero ranks, full ranks and oversized minors are included. No division, vertex, block-Jacobian, or coefficient-datum hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text:
For $f=	au_a(h_i)$, apply the shift-calculus coefficient formula with coefficient variables $W=T$, original shifted variables $Z$, shift vector $\phi(W)=W$, and $f(Z)$ independent of $W$. It gives $[Y^
u]f(T+Y)=\partial_T^
u f(T)/
u!$. Step 1 identifies this with $	au_a(\partial^
u h_i/
u!)$. Multiplication by $Y^\eta$ makes the coefficient in row $\gamma$ zero unless $\eta\le\gamma$, and otherwise the image of the displayed entry of $P_t(h)$. This proves the matrix comparison. The determinant permutation formula gives $	au_a(\det C)=\det(	au_a(C))$ for each square submatrix $C$. The extension of an ideal generated by these determinants is generated by their images, proving the asserted extension of $J_t(a)$, including oversized minors.

proof.text:
Put $Q_t=R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_d]/(Y)^{t+1}$, with $N_t$ monomials of degree at most $t$. It is free over $R$ on those monomials: dropping higher terms gives a representative, and a polynomial in $(Y)^{t+1}$ has no coefficient of degree at most $t$. Define $D_t(c)=\sum_{|
u|\le t}(\partial^
u c/
u!)Y^
u$. The iterated Leibniz rule gives $\partial^
u(cd)/
u!=\sum_{\alpha+ eta=
u}(\partial^\alpha c/\alpha!)(\partial^ eta d/ eta!)$, by induction on $|
u|$ from the derivation rule; thus $D_t$ is a ring homomorphism to $Q_t$. The column span $C_t(h)$ of $P_t(h)$ is exactly the ideal $(D_t(h_i))$ in $Q_t$, viewed as an $R$-submodule, since every multiplier in $Q_t$ is a finite $R$-linear combination of the $Y^\eta$. If $h'_j=\sum_i u_{ji}h_i$, then $D_t(h'_j)=\sum_iD_t(u_{ji})D_t(h_i)$; applying the reverse generator expressions gives $C_t(h')=C_t(h)$.

source.place: Agent truncated Taylor calculation; coefficient convolution and repeated Leibniz rule; BM Remarks 9.1, invariant jet-module interpretation.

proof.text: After evaluation at $b$, Step 1 identifies the columns with $T^\eta\tau_b(h_i)\bmod(T)^{t+1}$. Every formal multiplier has the same product modulo $(T)^{t+1}$ as its finite truncation. Consequently the evaluated column span is exactly the image of $K_b$ in the monomial vector space $L_b[[T]]/(T)^{t+1}$, of dimension $N_t$. The quotient-dimension lemma and the column-span characterization of rank give $H_b(t)=N_t-\operatorname{rank}_{L_b}P_t(h)(b)$. In particular $r_t(a)$ is the same for any finite generating family by Step 3. If $r_t(a)=N_t$, every $(r_t(a)+1)$-minor is oversized and $J_t(a)=0$ for every family. Otherwise put $k_t=N_t-r_t(a)-1\ge0$. Apply the presentation-independent kernel-row description to $R^{N_t}\twoheadrightarrow Q_t/C_t(h)$, identifying vectors with the transposed columns. It identifies $J_t(a)$ with $I_{k_t}$: determinants on arbitrary kernel vectors expand into linear combinations of determinants on generating columns, while the latter are among the former. Thus Step 3 proves generator independence also when $r_t(a)<N_t$.

source.place: Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), opening kernel-vector description; quotient dimension is Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank.

proof.text:
For every $b,t$, the rank/minor characterization and the definition of the minor ideal give
$$J_t(a)\subseteq\ker(R\to L_b)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{rank}P_t(h)(b)\le r_t(a)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ H_b(t)\ge H_a(t).$$
Indeed ideal containment means precisely that all its determinant generators vanish at $b$; rank is the largest size of a nonzero minor. The second equivalence is Step 4, with the same $N_t$ for every $b$. If $r_t(a)$ is full this is automatic on both sides, since $H_a(t)=0$.

source.place: BM Remarks 9.1, pp.275--276; direct rank/minor and quotient-dimension interpretation.

proof.text: Choose an open neighbourhood $U_0$ of $a$ on which the set $\mathcal H=\{H_b:b\in U_0\}$ is finite, as hypothesized. For each $F\in\mathcal H\setminus\{H_a\}$ choose a degree $t_F$ with $F(t_F)\ne H_a(t_F)$ and put $q_0=\max(\{0\}\cup\{t_F\})$. Fix any $q\ge q_0$. For each $0\le t\le q$ with $r_t(a)>0$, choose an $r_t(a)$-minor $\delta_t$ of $P_t(h)$ nonzero at $a$; the rank characterization supplies it. For rank zero put $\delta_t=1$. Define $V_q=U_0\cap\bigcap_{t=0}^qD(\delta_t)$, where $D(f)=\{b:f(b)\ne0\}$. These are open by the definition of the Zariski topology, and contain $a$. At $b\in V_q$, the chosen nonzero minors show $\operatorname{rank}P_t(h)(b)\ge r_t(a)$, hence $H_b(t)\le H_a(t)$ for $0\le t\le q$ by Step 4.

source.place: Tags 00DZ (definition-spectrum-ring) and 00E1 (definition-Zariski-topology); agent finite-witness determinant-open argument following BM Remarks 9.1 and 9.5(2).

proof.text: If $b\in V_q$ satisfies all the minor-ideal conditions through $q$, Step 5 and Step 6 imply $H_b(t)=H_a(t)$ for every $0\le t\le q$. If $H_b\ne H_a$, its chosen witness $t_{H_b}\le q_0\le q$ contradicts this equality. Thus $H_b=H_a$. Conversely that equality implies every minor condition, by Step 5, even without shrinking. This proves the two sets are equal for every $q\ge q_0$. If $\mathcal H=\{H_a\}$ take $q_0=0$. If the generators are empty, every column span is zero and $J_t=0$, while $H_b(t)=N_t$ everywhere. If $I=R$, the evaluated column span is full and $H_b=0$ everywhere. The argument includes $d=0$, $a\notin X$, zero ranks, and oversized minors; at nonclosed points it retains the same $d$ variables and uses only evaluation in $\kappa(b)$, never the completion of $\mathcal O_{U,b}$ with fewer parameters.
